baseline_models.focus_anchor: The command أَدُّوا ... عِبَادَ اللَّهِ followed by رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The imperative treats the people as a due trust to be rendered, not cargo to be newly acquired. Their slave-status is the contested relation, God's service is the counterclaim, and the trustworthy messenger is the accredited recipient and guarantor.

activation_trace.role: Fulfilling a due or trust makes the imperative a restitution rather than a neutral handover.
Owned slave-status supplies the human relation whose legitimacy the requested restitution contests.
The worshipped one supplies the servants' prior divine claim against human possession.
Messenger and carried message make the speaker an authorized representative rather than a private claimant.
Settled security and trust make the envoy a guarantor of the handover's safety.

changed_reading.before: Hand God's servants over to me.
changed_reading.after: Discharge a human trust to its accredited, safe recipient: stop holding God's servants as transferable property and render what is due.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The directional construction أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ and the speaker's self-designation as رَسُول.
baseline_models.mechanism: Delivery reaches a destination, while a messenger is himself one sent forth. The speaker can therefore be a relay point in an onward release rather than the terminal owner of the people delivered to him.

activation_trace.role: Arrival at a destination makes إِلَيَّ a transfer node whose endpoint need not be permanent possession.
Being sent forth and released gives the recipient an intrinsically onward-moving role.
The envoy function turns personal reception into a mediated transfer under another sender's authority.
Trustworthy safe-conduct makes the relay a protected passage rather than a change of masters.

changed_reading.before: Transfer the servants from your custody into mine.
changed_reading.after: Bring them through to an accredited transit point so that the one already sent can carry them onward into release.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The exact adjacency أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ and the accusative phrase عِبَادَ اللَّهِ, which can remain the object or be heard as a vocative.
baseline_models.mechanism: The branch explicitly licenses أَدَّ إِلَى as giving ear. If عِبَادَ اللَّهِ is heard vocatively rather than as the transferred object, the same wording addresses the hearers as God's servants and asks them to heed an envoy whose report merits trusting assent. This reading coexists with, rather than cancels, the object reading.

activation_trace.role: Offering one's hearing activates a direct 'give ear to me' value in the adjacent prepositional construction.
Worship and submissive obedience let 'servants of God' name the addressed hearers' proper allegiance.
Divine worship makes the vocative an identity claim directed at the audience, not only a possessor phrase.
Messenger and message supply the speech-content to which the audience is asked to listen.
Trusting assent turns 'trustworthy' into a reason to accept the heard report.

changed_reading.before: Deliver God's servants to me; I am a trustworthy messenger.
changed_reading.after: O servants of God, give ear and heed to me; I carry a message worthy of assent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding sequence supplies an enacted decree, a fixed entitlement, a secure station, and protection from harm. Together they turn the focus handover into fulfillment of an established right whose intended result is protected security.

activation_trace.role: Rendering a due anchors the contextual decree and right in the focus imperative.
Slave-status identifies the concrete human claim that the obligation requires the holders to discharge.
A written fixing that makes a judgment obligatory supplies the decree-frame for the demanded performance.
A binding entitlement supplies the legal direction from obligation to restitution.
Settled security turns the messenger's trustworthiness into the destination-state of the transferred servants.
Protection that repels harm supplies the practical outcome promised by safe restitution.

structural_cues: 44:2-4 frames the surah with a clarifying writ and differentiated command.
44:51-56 places security and protection at the successful end of the movement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies obligation, fixed right, security, and protection; I infer that they retrospectively specify what must be 'rendered' and why. A live alternative is a political surrender with no technical legal force.

changed_reading.before: The speaker asks for a trustworthy handover.
changed_reading.after: The holders are ordered to satisfy a pre-existing human entitlement under safe-conduct, with protected security as the handover's designed result.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later servants travel by night, are pursued, pass through an open calm gap, and are separated into rescue. That route resolves إِلَيَّ as the first handoff in an escape chain, not the final destination of ownership.

activation_trace.role: Bringing through to a destination anchors the later route in the focus act of delivery.
Being sent forth makes the messenger the moving relay who receives and then leads onward.
Night travel supplies the next leg after delivery to the messenger.
The repeated servant-group identifies the travelers as the people requested in the focus.
Following and pursuit make the transfer an urgent extraction rather than a settled custody change.
A broad open gap supplies the spatial aperture through which the delivered group continues.
Rescue by separation names the route's outcome and clarifies the handoff as liberation.

structural_cues: 44:23 repeats the servant-group and immediately gives it a night itinerary.
44:24-30 converts that itinerary into passage, pursuit, and rescue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the same group, travel, pursuit, an opening, and rescue; I supply the retrospective arrow from 'to me' to that route. The live alternative is that the focus endpoint is complete and the later journey is merely subsequent.

changed_reading.before: Bring the servants to the speaker as destination.
changed_reading.after: Bring them to the speaker as the first safe node of a night extraction whose real endpoint is separation from captivity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, the messenger brings a cogent authority, asks for belief, and permits withdrawal if belief is refused. This reception-oriented sequence strengthens the alternative vocative parse: the hearers are called God's servants and asked to attend to a trustworthy message.

activation_trace.role: Giving ear anchors the reception sequence directly in the focus imperative.
The carried message supplies what the vocatively addressed hearers are to receive.
Cogent authority makes the messenger's address evidence to be heard and evaluated.
Trusting assent makes belief in the speaker the response sought by the auditory command.
Withdrawal into a separate side supplies the non-assent branch of the proposed hearing encounter.

structural_cues: 44:18-21 moves from messenger identity to clear authority, belief, and withdrawal.
44:23 then reopens the competing object reading by moving a servant-group.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies proof, belief, and withdrawal after the focus; I infer that this progression turns the imperative into an auditory decision point. The object-transfer reading remains live and gains separate support at 44:23.

changed_reading.before: The imperative concerns only transfer of a third-party group.
changed_reading.after: It also directly addresses the rulers as servants of God: hear the accredited message and decide whether to assent or withdraw.

context_deltas.mechanism: The ban on self-exaltation against God, Pharaoh's excessive highness, and the later image of violent dragging expose a sovereignty contest inside عِبَادَ اللَّهِ. Rendering the servants becomes an undoing of human domination that has trespassed on divine allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Making someone a slave exposes the active domination that the focus command can require its holders to reverse.
Divine worship supplies the allegiance against which human enslavement becomes a sovereignty violation.
Arrogant self-magnification names the posture that refuses to relinquish God's servants.
Exceeding the limit turns Pharaoh's highness into unlawful overreach rather than mere rank.
Violent coercive dragging supplies a later mirror of domination forcibly reversed upon its practitioner.

structural_cues: 44:19 places the prohibition of elevation against God immediately after the demand for God's servants.
44:31 names Pharaoh's height as excess, while 44:47 later reverses coercive movement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies enslavement, divine allegiance, arrogant elevation, excess, and violent dragging; I infer a reversal from usurped mastery to relinquishment. A live alternative is a narrower custody dispute without a general sovereignty mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Return a group held by the ruler.
changed_reading.after: Renounce the ruler's enacted claim to mastery: rendering God's servants is a concrete reversal of self-exaltation against God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sequence sharply distinguishes capture and violent dragging from secure station. Against that contrast, أَدُّوا and أَمِين specify not merely who moves but the ethical mode of movement: due performance under trust rather than seizure under force.

activation_trace.role: Fulfilling a trust supplies the noncoercive transfer mode against which later seizure is contrasted.
Safe trust makes protection, not force, the messenger's governing transfer condition.
Capture and arrest supply the coercive transfer mode absent from the focus verb.
Dragging by force intensifies the lexical contrast between compelled seizure and due delivery.
The secure station confirms safety as the positive destination opposed to coercive transport.

structural_cues: 44:47 uses an explicit take-and-drag sequence for coercive movement.
44:51 answers that scene with a secure station using the same root as the focus adjective.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two different movement lexicons and a later secure endpoint; I infer an ethical contrast that qualifies the focus handover. The live alternative is that the later scenes are unrelated destinations, not a comment on transfer mode.

changed_reading.before: Any effective transfer of the servants could satisfy the command.
changed_reading.after: Only a trust-like, safety-governed release fits the focus diction; capture and violent dragging belong to its punitive opposite.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing description of eased language, the tongue as message-delivery, and reminder loops back to the focus branch of offering one's hearing. It makes the messenger's request a communicative channel: speech is made deliverable so that hearing can become remembrance.

activation_trace.role: Offering hearing anchors the late language-and-reminder sequence in the focus construction.
The messenger's carried speech supplies the content that travels through the linguistic channel.
Opening ease after difficulty makes the message accessible at the sending side of the channel.
The tongue as an instrument for conveying a message directly links speech production to messenger function.
Reminder supplies the intended receiving-side effect of giving ear.

structural_cues: 44:58 closes the discourse by joining linguistic ease to possible remembrance.
The focus already joins an imperative of reception to messenger identity and trust.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies linguistic ease, message-delivery, and reminder; I infer a channel from spoken delivery to offered hearing to remembered content. The material handover remains the syntactically direct alternative.

changed_reading.before: The messenger's trustworthiness only guarantees a physical handover.
changed_reading.after: It also guarantees a communicative handoff: accessible speech asks for an opened ear so that the message can arrive as remembrance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant split target for the focus verb and is morphologically distant from the surface imperative. It remains anchored to word 2 and coheres with the displacement of enslavement by trusted relation. Downstream prose should call it an affective overlay or latent reaffiliation image, never a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The packet's secondary mapped target for أَدُّوا, read alongside enslaving عِبَاد and trustworthy أَمِين.

activation_trace.role: Affectionate attachment turns the destination into a possible reaffiliation under care rather than acquisition.
Enslavement supplies the coercive relation that an affective reaffiliation would displace.
Settled trust supplies the secure relational quality that keeps the affective overlay tied to the verse.

changed_reading.before: The demanded release is solely juridical and spatial.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, release also repairs affiliation: people are moved out of coerced ownership toward a trusted bond of care.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the serial-dying branch belongs to a distant idiomatic extension and the focus form ordinarily demands delivery. It remains packet-anchored at word 2 and becomes live when the context advances through caused death, overwhelming seizure, and drowning. Downstream prose should render it only as a dark echo or abductive foreshadowing: refusal to release opens a death-sequence, not that أَدُّوا literally means 'die successively' here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The serial-dying branch attached to focus word 2, under a context that unfolds successive forms of lethal consequence.

activation_trace.role: Successive dying casts a contained consequence-shadow behind the demand to deliver the servants.
Causing life to depart supplies the first explicit lethal capacity in the contextual progression.
Overwhelming seizure supplies the violent turn that follows repeated refusal.
Drowning as killing gives the shadow-sequence a concrete collective culmination.

changed_reading.before: The command requests release without encoding a consequence path.
changed_reading.after: As a contained echo, it is also an ultimatum at a fork: render the servants, or refusal will unfold into successive lethal reversals.

strongest_changes: The object reading became restitution of a due human trust under safe-conduct, not a neutral transfer of property.
The later night journey and rescue changed إِلَيَّ from terminal possession into the first relay of an extraction route.
A coexisting vocative reading emerged: 'O servants of God, give ear to me,' strengthened by the proof-belief-withdrawal sequence and the closing language-reminder loop.
The domination and forced-movement mirrors made the handover a reversal of usurped mastery and distinguished trusted release from coercive seizure.
summary.what_was_special: The same focus construction sustained two opposed but traceable grammars: a servant-group delivered to the messenger and hearers addressed as God's servants. Context did not collapse them; 44:23-30 strengthened the first while 44:19-21 and 44:58 strengthened the second. The split mapping also preserved affective and fatal shadows that a conservative synthesis would discard.
remaining_uncertainties: The overt accusative عِبَادَ strongly favors a direct object but can also support an elided-vocative analysis; the packet does not force one syntax.
The relay reading depends on letting later itinerary retrospectively qualify إِلَيَّ rather than treating the speaker as a complete endpoint.
The affective split-target and serial-death activations are deliberately contained overlays because their morphology and directional arrows remain distant.
